subject: Trouble using ModavgPred with a continuous and categorical interaction

messages.author: 198c44d635827adf
messages.subject: Trouble using ModavgPred with a continuous and categorical interaction
parts:
Dear group,

I am having trouble obtaining predicted estimates for a N-mixture model containing a continuous and categorical variable using modavgPred. My categorical variable is a dummy variable for archery season. Below is the model formula and coefficients    

Call:

pcount(formula = ~People ~ Slope * Archery + MeanNDVI * Archery +

    FireDist * Archery, data = UMF, K = 200)

 

Abundance:

                 Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)

(Intercept)       -0.6215 0.478 -1.300  0.1935

Slope             -0.3589 0.290 -1.236  0.2166

Archery            0.8426 0.434  1.941  0.0523

MeanNDVI           0.9437 0.447  2.112  0.0347

FireDist           0.0668 0.234  0.285  0.7755

Slope:Archery      0.4457 0.352  1.265  0.2058

Archery:MeanNDVI  -0.8282 0.502 -1.648  0.0993

Archery:FireDist   0.0532 0.318  0.167  0.8673

 

Detection:

            Estimate    SE      z  P(>|z|)

(Intercept)   -4.088 0.405 -10.08 6.69e-24

People        -0.786 0.441  -1.78 7.46e-02

 

I have tried following the code in the book but I keep getting the attached results. Below is the code I am using to try to predict the interaction between MeanNDVI and archery season on abundance.

 MeanNDVI.orig=seq(min(MCArcheryComCovars$MeanNDVI),max(MCArcheryComCovars$MeanNDVI), length.out=100)

MeanNDVI.mean=mean(MCArcheryComCovars$MeanNDVI)

MeanNDVI.sd=sd(MCArcheryComCovars$MeanNDVI)

MeanNDVI.std=(MeanNDVI.orig-MeanNDVI.mean)/MeanNDVI.sd

 

newData2=data.frame(Slope=0,FireDist=0, HorseDistCenter=0, AveRdDist=0,

                    MeanNDVI=MeanNDVI.std,People=People.std, Date=0, Archery=factor("1",levels = c(0,1)) )

 

NDVI.predict=modavgPred(cand.set = List, newdata = newData2, parm.type='lambda',

                         level=0.85, type="response")

 

plot(MeanNDVI.orig,NDVI.predict$mod.avg.pred,type="l",lwd=2,col="blue", xlab="NDVI",

     ylab="Abundance", las=1, ylim=c(0,5), frame=F)

 

Help figuring out what I am doing wrong would be greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you,

 

Ryan Platte

Hi Ryan (this would be more appropriate to the unmarked Google forum),

If you fit an interaction in your model and want to illustrate it in
your plot of predictions, your data frame should vary your meanNDVI
numeric vector with both Archery == 1 and Archery == 0. In other words,
create a data frame with expand.grid( ):

newDats <- expand.grid(MeanNDVI = MeanNDVI.std,
Archery = factor(c("0", "1"),levels = c(0,1)))

And then add the other variables at their mean
newDats$Slope <- 0
newDats$FireDist <- 0
newDats$HorseDistCenter <- 0
newDats$AveRdDist <- 0
newDats$Date <- 0

Then make your predictions:
NDVI.predict <-modavgPred(cand.set = List, newdata = newData2,

Best,

Marc

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Trouble using ModavgPred with a continuous and categorical interaction
parts:
Ryan,

Your original plot looks correct to me based on your model results.

Ignoring covariates unrelated to your question, your equation for abundance will look like this (where x is your data):

y = exp(Intercept + Archery*x_archery + meanNDVI*x_ndvi + Archery:MeanNDVI*x_archery*x_meanNDVI)

Your equation at an Archery site  (x_archery = 1) will be

y = exp(-0.62 + 0.84 * (1) + 0.94 * x_ndvi + -0.83 * (1) * x_ndvi)

or

y = exp(0.22 + 0.11 * x_ndvi)

So there is still a positive relationship (0.11) with NDVI, it's just not as strong as sites that where preArchery, which again matches your figure.

Ken
